activities.name: Acatenango Overnight Volcano Camp
activities.description: Grind up the steep flanks of the dormant Acatenango volcano to a high-altitude base camp on the ridge, then spend the night watching the neighboring Volcán de Fuego erupt violently in real time — glowing lava bombs arcing into the darkness and ash columns lit orange from below. One of the most visceral natural experiences in Central America.
activities.duration_note: 2 days / 1 night. Night temperatures drop below freezing at camp — heavy layers essential. Altitude sickness common above 3,500m

activities.name: Pacaya Volcano Day Hike
activities.description: Hike across dramatic fields of cooled black lava rock and active thermal vents on the slopes of Pacaya — roasting marshmallows over natural geothermal heat and walking right up to lava flows. One of the most accessible active volcano experiences in the world.
activities.duration_note: Includes shuttle transport and mandatory guide. Cash only for park entry

activities.name: Antigua Colonial Ruins Crawl
activities.description: Wander through the hauntingly beautiful earthquake-shattered ruins of Antigua's colonial convents, cathedrals, and monasteries — collapsed by the 1773 Santa Marta earthquakes and left deliberately unrestored, with bougainvillea growing through broken arches and grass carpeting former nave floors.
activities.duration_note: Combined entry fees for multiple ruins sites — cash only

activities.name: Iximché Kaqchikel Maya Ruins
activities.description: Explore the fortified hilltop ruins of Iximché — the 15th-century capital of the Kaqchikel Maya kingdom — where the plazas, ball courts, and twin-temple pyramids still host active Maya spiritual ceremonies. Smoke rising from ritual fire altars on weekends makes this one of Guatemala's most living archaeological sites.
activities.duration_note: Price includes foreigner entry fee (Q50) plus private transport from Antigua (Q300). Active ceremonial altars — observe respectfully

activities.name: Coffee & Macadamia Farm Estate Tour
activities.description: Tour the lush agricultural estates surrounding Antigua — walking through shade-grown coffee plantations, learning the full bean-to-cup process from cherry picking to roasting, tasting single-origin espresso at altitude, and sampling macadamia-based products from the valley's productive nut farms.

activities.name: Pepián & Rellenitos at Mercado Central
activities.description: Eat Guatemala's national dish at a comedor inside the Mercado Central — Pepián, a dark, complex chicken stew thickened with toasted pumpkin seeds, sesame, and dried chiles that has been cooked the same way for 500 years — then finish with Rellenitos, fried plantain balls stuffed with sweet black beans and dusted with sugar.

activities.name: Ulew Speakeasy & Antigua Brewing Company
activities.description: Start at Ulew — a speakeasy hidden behind a vintage phone booth inside a pizzeria, where no-menu mixologists craft cocktails entirely around your flavor profile — then move to the Antigua Brewing Company's expansive rooftop deck for craft beers with a direct view of the illuminated cones of Agua, Fuego, and Acatenango volcanoes.

activities.name: Cafe No Sé — Mezcal Dive Bar & Live Music
activities.description: Duck into Cafe No Sé — Antigua's most legendary candlelit dive bar and the birthplace of Ilegal Mezcal, now exported worldwide. Tiny, dark, and atmospheric, with intimate live acoustic sets and a devoted mix of expats, travelers, and locals crowded around the wooden bar.

activities.name: Indian Nose Sunrise Trek
activities.description: Make a steep pre-dawn ascent up the dramatic ridge profile of Nariz del Indio — Indian Nose — arriving at the summit as the sun rises over the three volcanoes of Lake Atitlán, painting the entire caldera in amber and pink light in one of the most spectacular sunrise views in Central America.
activities.duration_note: Guided with morning transport included — depart by 4:00 AM for sunrise

activities.name: San Juan La Laguna Indigenous Art & Weaving Tour
activities.description: Walk through San Juan La Laguna — Atitlán's premier arts village — visiting active cooperatives where Tz'utujil women weave intricate textiles on backstrap looms using natural dyes extracted from cochineal insects, indigo plants, and local flowers in techniques unchanged for centuries.
activities.duration_note: Tip cooperative artisans directly — most income goes straight to the weavers

activities.name: Chichicastenango Indigenous Market Day
activities.description: Immerse yourself in Latin America's largest and most atmospheric traditional open-air market — held every Thursday and Sunday in Chichicastenango — where thousands of Maya highland artisans sell handwoven textiles, jade, masks, and ceramics under clouds of copal incense smoke rising from the steps of the Santo Tomás church.
activities.duration_note: Thursdays and Sundays only. Price includes round-trip tourist shuttle

activities.name: Fuentes Georginas Cloud Forest Hot Springs
activities.description: Soak in naturally heated volcanic hot spring pools tucked into a mist-shrouded cloud forest canyon high above Quetzaltenango — the sulfur-rich thermal waters surrounded by fern-draped walls and ancient trees, with temperatures cooling as altitude climbs.
activities.duration_note: Price includes entry (Q60) plus tuk-tuk or shuttle transport from Xela (Q150)

activities.name: Lake Atitlán Kayaking & Cliff Jumping
activities.description: Paddle across the glassy early-morning waters of Lake Atitlán between the villages of Santa Cruz and San Marcos — the three volcanoes reflected perfectly in the still surface — then leap off 7-meter wooden cliff jump platforms into the deep, cool caldera lake.
activities.location: Santa Cruz / San Marcos La Laguna, Sololá
activities.duration_note: Go before 11:00 AM — the Xocomil afternoon winds make the lake choppy by midday

activities.name: Patarasca Lake Fish & Jocón Stew
activities.description: Taste the Western Highlands' two most distinct dishes — Patarasca, fresh lake fish seasoned with wild tomatoes and wrapped in maxán leaves to grill over wood embers, and Jocón, a tangy green chicken stew vivid with tomatillos, cilantro, and green peppers — at a highland comedor with handmade tortillas.

activities.name: Sublime San Pedro & The Clover Panajachel
activities.description: Hit San Pedro La Laguna's liveliest lakefront venue — Sublime — for dance music and a social backpacker crowd, then cross to Panajachel's The Clover Irish pub on Calle Santander for local acoustic musicians and cold regional drafts. Two very different ends of Atitlán's nightlife spectrum on the same evening.

activities.name: Tikal Sunrise Archaeological Expedition
activities.description: Hike through Tikal's jungle in total darkness before dawn, guided only by headlamp, to climb Temple IV as howler monkeys erupt in their prehistoric dawn chorus — watching the sun slowly illuminate the pyramid tops emerging from the unbroken forest canopy in one of the most extraordinary archaeological experiences on Earth.
activities.duration_note: Price includes day ticket (Q150), sunrise permit (Q100), and guide (Q100). Tickets must be purchased in advance at Banrural bank in Flores or online — cannot buy at park gate. Bring passport

activities.name: Yaxhá Lakeside Ruins Sunset Expedition
activities.description: Explore the lesser-visited lakeside Maya city of Yaxhá — a vast, forested site of over 500 structures — climbing Temple 216 for a panoramic golden hour view over the jungle and twin lagoons below. Far fewer crowds than Tikal with an equally majestic atmosphere.
activities.duration_note: Price includes entry (Q80) plus shared shuttle from Flores (Q250)

activities.name: Crater Azul River & Blue Pool Boat Trek
activities.description: Journey deep down winding jungle river channels by boat to reach Crater Azul — a stunning oasis of electric-blue, crystal-clear freshwater pools hidden in the Petén lowlands, where you swim through natural gardens of aquatic plants in water of impossible clarity.
activities.duration_note: Priced per person based on sharing a boat (Q1,200–1,500 per boat split among passengers). Full day including transit

activities.name: El Mirador Deep Jungle Trek Expedition
activities.description: Trek deep into the virtually roadless northern Petén jungle to reach El Mirador — home to La Danta, one of the largest pyramids ever built by volume, still mostly buried under centuries of jungle growth. A physically demanding, genuinely remote wilderness expedition through ancient Maya heartland.
activities.duration_note: 5 days / 4 nights jungle hike. Helicopter charter also available (~$520+ USD for 1 day). Strong physical fitness required. All meals, guides, and mules included in trek packages

activities.name: Flores Island Walking Loop & Lake Swimming
activities.description: Stroll the charming pastel-painted colonial streets of Flores — a small island city connected to the mainland by a single causeway, sitting in the middle of Lake Petén Itzá — stopping to swim off the public wooden dock platforms that extend into the warm lake.
activities.duration_note: Free — bring cash for food and drinks from boardwalk stalls

activities.name: Flores Island Waterfront Night Food Stalls
activities.description: Graze the evening food stalls on the northern waterfront boardwalk of Flores island — local home cooks selling Bolitos de Chaya (savory corn-chaya dough balls stuffed with pork), handmade empanadas, and traditional drinks as the sun sets over Lake Petén Itzá behind them.

activities.name: Sky Bar Rooftop & San Telmo Mezcal Lounge
activities.description: Catch happy hour at Flores' Sky Bar rooftop for sweeping views over Lake Petén Itzá at sunset, then move to San Telmo — an eccentric, artistically decorated bohemian café and lounge right on the water serving artisanal mezcals, craft beers, and a creative, international crowd.

activities.name: Semuc Champey Tiered Pools & K'anba Cave
activities.description: Swim in the extraordinary tiered turquoise limestone pools of Semuc Champey — a natural bridge of calcium carbonate spanning a jungle river gorge — then navigate the pitch-black K'anba river cave system holding only a lit wax candle, crawling through chambers and swimming underground pools.
activities.duration_note: Price includes park entry (Q50) and cave entry with guide (Q60). Getting here involves hours of mountain switchbacks then an open-air 4x4 truck ride — prepare for motion sickness. Withdraw cash in Cobán beforehand

activities.name: Río Dulce Jungle Canyon Boat Cruise
activities.description: Board a boat at Fronteras and drift down the spectacular Río Dulce canyon — sheer jungle walls rising 100 meters on both sides, with hot spring waterfalls trickling into the river, tropical birds overhead, and water lilies carpeting the surface — arriving at the Caribbean Garífuna town of Livingston.

activities.name: Livingston Garífuna Culture Walking Tour
activities.description: Explore Livingston — Guatemala's only Caribbean enclave, accessible only by water — home to the Garífuna people, an Afro-indigenous community with their own unique language, punta drumming tradition, and culinary identity entirely distinct from the rest of Guatemala.
activities.duration_note: Village walks are free — accessible only by boat from Río Dulce or Punta Gorda, Belize

activities.name: El Paredón Pacific Surf Session
activities.description: Surf the powerful black volcanic sand beach breaks of El Paredón — Guatemala's rapidly growing Pacific eco-surf enclave, where the strong Pacific swells produce consistent, punchy waves perfect for intermediate surfers on a dramatic, development-free coastline.
activities.duration_note: Powerful rip currents — consult local surf instructors before going out alone. Price per hour for board rental and lesson

activities.name: Bioluminescent Mangrove Night Kayak
activities.description: Paddle through a dark mangrove forest channel after nightfall as your paddle strokes ignite brilliant blue-white bioluminescent plankton in the water around you — every stroke leaving trails of living light in one of Guatemala's most magical and underrated natural experiences.
activities.duration_note: Guided night excursion only — best on moonless nights for maximum bioluminescence visibility

activities.name: Kak'ik Turkey Soup & Tapado Caribbean Stew
activities.description: Try the ancient Mayan Kak'ik in Alta Verapaz — a ceremonial turkey soup deeply spiced with coriander, achiote, and dried chiles that has been prepared the same way since pre-Columbian times — then contrast it with Livingston's Tapado, a rich Caribbean seafood coconut broth packed with whole crab, shrimp, and plantains.

activities.name: Driftwood Trooper Beach Bar & Buga Mama Punta Night
activities.description: Hit the Driftwood Trooper at El Paredón for happy hour beach volleyball under stadium lights and a social surf crowd, then if in Livingston head to Buga Mama — a waterfront community collective showcasing live Punta drumming and dance performances, the heartbeat rhythm of Garífuna culture.
